data.name: Babun
data.gender_notes: Babun is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who is devoted to Lord Shiva. In Hindu mythology, Shiva is the God of destruction, time, and regeneration. Devotees of Shiva are often referred to as Babas or Babas, reflecting their deep spiritual connection. The name Babun carries the meaning “Lord Shiva's devotee” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Babun usually hope their child will grow to embody lord shiva's devotee and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of devotion and dedication to the divine.
data.etymology: Babun belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord Shiva's devotee.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Babun total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name Sakuna is of Japanese origin, and is commonly used in Japanese folklore for the goddess of rice and the patron deity of agriculture. It reflects her role in providing food security to communities.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Sakuna embodies the gratitude and connection to the natural world, particularly through agriculture, which is deeply enshrined in Japanese spiritual practices.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Babun in Hindu tradition can be symbolically interpreted as 'One who serves the Divine as a devotee and babbler, spreading the sacred words of God'. Alternatively, it can be seen as one who is 'Blessed by Baba (Father) or God, cherished and protected'.

historical_references.reference: Babur, the founder of the Mughal Empire in India, was born in 1483 in Uzbekistan. He was a Timurid prince and a descendant of Genghis Khan.

Babur invaded India in 1526 with an army of 12,000 men and defeated the last ruler of the Delhi Sultanate, Ibrahim Lodhi, in the Battle of Panipat. This marked the beginning of the Mughal Empire in India.
historical_references.context: Babur's conquest of India and founding of the Mughal Empire
